g.text: DESIGN MINDS · PREPRESS GRAPHIC RESEARCH SCHEMATICS · DAY 021
THE MOIRÉ ROSETTE & HALFTONE SCREEN INTERFERENCE
AM SCREEN ANGLES (15°/45°/75°) · BEAT FREQUENCY OPTICAL KINETICS · KARL GERSTNER PROGRAMMED TYPOGRAPHY
30° Angular Separation Matrix to Prevent Low-Frequency Moiré
Yields high-frequency Rosette dots (~0.12mm) imperceptible to the naked eye.
SECTION 02: MOIRÉ BEAT WAVELENGTH VS. MISREGISTRATION ANGLE
Spatial Frequency Interference Equation: Wavelength Spikes as Δθ → 0°
THE OPTICAL BEAT FREQUENCY THEOREM (RAYLEIGH & BRAGG):
When two spatial frequencies overlap, spatial beating produces macro-ripples.
At Δθ = 0°, f_beat collapses to 0 (infinite stripe width); at 30°, f_beat > 120 LPI (invisible).
Microscopic Halftone Dot Rosettes vs. Acute Angle Moiré Rhomboids
150 LPI Newspaper: Rosette cell = 0.17mm (Blends at 35cm viewing distance)
Coarse 30 LPI Poster: Rosette visible as decorative modernist texture
SECTION 04: KARL GERSTNER PROGRAMMED MOIRÉ TYPOGRAPHY
Overlaying Dynamic Line Grids over Grotesk Letterforms to Generate Kinetic Optical Vibration
THE KINETIC ILLUSION OF MOIRÉ TYPOGRAPHY:
As the reader shifts their head or scrolls the viewport, the angular discrepancy
causes the dark moiré fringes to sweep across the word PROGRAMME at 12× scroll velocity,
producing an organic optical shimmer without a single line of CSS keyframe animation.
Karl Gerstner: "Typography is the art of producing literature by mechanical means."
